sights.address: Lornie Road / Kheam Hock Road, Novena, Singapore
sights.w: Singapore's largest Chinese cemetery and reputedly the largest outside China: ~100,000 graves on 70–86 ha of overgrown hills, opened as a municipal cemetery on 1 Jan 1922 and closed to burials in 1973. Grand Peranakan and Hokkien tombs with Sikh guardian statues and tiled tablets; partly exhumed in 2012–13 for a highway, which sparked a heritage campaign that now runs free guided walks.
sights.k: Free; join a Brownies heritage walk (weekends); bring insect repellent

sights.w: A former nutmeg plantation turned early-1900s residential quarter for the wealthy, conserved by URA on 7 Jul 1989: a stretch of mostly two-storey Late and Art Deco-style terrace houses raised above the road on flights of steps, with recessed verandahs and geometric ventilation blocks — several restorations have won URA Architectural Heritage Awards. On NHB's Orchard Heritage Trail, which also points out the c.1926 Tan Chin Tuan Mansion with its bell-shaped turret.
sights.k: Free; private homes — view from the street

sights.w: A 1926 mansion at the junction of Cairnhill Road and Cairnhill Circle, built in the rubber-boom era and later home of OCBC chairman and philanthropist Tan Chin Tuan — note the tower with its bell-shaped turret and the columned porch. Conserved by URA and pointed out on NHB's Orchard Heritage Trail; now fronting a condominium.
